subject: Stakeholder mapping & procurement path — Acme Commerce
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme-commerce.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps (stakeholder mapping)

Hi Samantha — great speaking with you earlier. Thanks for walking us through the use case (personalization + search re-rank) and the current pain: bursty traffic during campaign drops and high per-token cost on your side. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Call recap:
- Primary use cases: dynamic content re-ranking (homepage, email), on-demand personalization snippets for campaigns.
- Current infra: mixed managed endpoints + internal LLM infra; procurement wants a single vendor SLA for inference.
- Key decision criteria: latency (95th < 200ms), predictable cost, security controls (SAML, audit logs), ability to pin model versions for rollout.

Asks from your side:
- Can you share a short org chart (who owns procurement, security/legal, product engineering, and campaign ops)?
- Who is the economic buyer for inference spend?
- Any required security/compliance docs or split-of-data concerns we should preemptively gather?

Proposed next steps: 
1) If you can send the org chart/decision chain, we’ll map recommended stakeholders and a suggested intro sequence.
2) Connor will draft a short MOP/technical summary (latency/cost SLOs + integrations) for procurement/security.
3) Rishi will prepare a high-level pricing ballpark and reserved capacity options to help the procurement conversation.

Attachments: I’ve attached a suggested stakeholder mapping template and a blank org-chart template (Acme_org_chart_v3.pdf, MAP_Remarks_Marissa.docx).

Would you be able to share the org chart and indicate who we should loop in from Procurement and Legal? Happy to coordinate a 30-min procurement + security intro next week if that helps.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme-commerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@acme-commerce.com>, procurement@acme-commerce.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps (stakeholder mapping)

Thanks Marissa — nice recap and thanks for the template. Attaching our org snapshot (see Acme_org_chart_v3.pdf). A few notes: 

- Economic buyer: Carlos Ruiz (VP Finance) — he owns vendor spend over $250k.
- Procurement point: procurement@acme-commerce.com (I copied them).
- Security/Legal: Anita Sharma (Head of Security & Legal) — she likes to review any data flow diagrams and vendor SOC2 evidence up front.

Quick answers to your asks: I’m attaching the basic org chart. The people you’ll want to meet: 
- Carlos Ruiz (finance) — evaluates ROI and total cost of ownership; wants a 1-2 slide cost model.
- Anita Sharma (security/legal) — will request SOC2 + data handling questionnaire.
- Derek Park (Engineering Manager, Search) — technical owner for integration and rollout.

We’d appreciate a 1-pager for procurement and a short technical appendix for Anita that outlines where customer data touches Redwood systems and what options we have for private deployment.

Can we do a joint procurement + security intro on Wed 5/13 at 10am PT? I can set the invite if that time works.

Best,
Samantha
Director of Product Ops | Acme Commerce
Samantha.Li@acme-commerce.com

Thanks Samantha — this is perfect. I’ve updated the stakeholder mapping template with the names you shared and attached it (MAP_Remarks_Marissa.docx). A few clarifications and what we’ll bring to the Wed 5/13 meeting: 

Clarifications: 
- Carlos — for the procurement conversation, would you prefer a committed reserved capacity proposal (monthly/annual) vs a consumption-first pricing example? We can bring both, but want to emphasize the cost predict-offs.
- Anita — we will attach our SOC 2 summary and a short data flow diagram that outlines where customer data is processed, what is encrypted, and options for private deployment.

What we’ll bring to Wed: 
- 1-page procurement summary (pricing bands, reserved vs. on-demand economics, typical savings examples) — Rishi
- Technical appendix (data flow + integration checklist) — Connor
- Suggested rollout and canary plan + success criteria for the pilot (latency targets, token volume assumptions) — Marissa

If Wed 5/13 10am PT works, Samantha, please send the invite and include a short agenda. Also, let us know if Anita wants the SOC2 + data flow diagram beforehand (we can send as a pre-read).

Thanks all — looking forward to the intro.

—
Marissa

Subject: Internal: next steps for ACME procurement intro

Internal notes — quick checklist before Wed: 
- Rishi: draft 1-pager pricing (reserved vs on-demand + example TCO for 6-month pilot). Aim for one slide + supporting numbers. Please include a quick sensitivity table (token volume variance).
- Connor: technical appendix + short data flow diagram (we should include both hosted and private deployment notes). Attach as PDF for pre-read.
- Monica: can you prep a short set of questions for Anita around encryption keys / KMS and any required audit log retention windows?
- I’ll own the meeting agenda and pilot success criteria.

Goal: be procurement-ready with clear asks and a pricing path. I’ll send drafts to the thread by EOD Tuesday for review.

—Marissa
